- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly.
- When sentiment is negative (≤-0.5) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, especially if recent price is falling.
- After sharp price spikes, model frequently overshoots in the next 5–10 days; apply a downward correction of 2–5% for the following 3–7 days.
- If model forecast is significantly above true outcome (e.g., >10% higher), check sentiment for bullish bias — if present, reduce forecast by 1–3% per day until sentiment shifts.
- If model forecast is significantly below true outcome (e.g., >10% lower), check sentiment for bearish bias — if present, increase forecast by 1–3% per day until sentiment shifts.
- Mean reversion is common in 10–15 day horizons; if forecast is >15% above recent 5-day average, reduce by 1–2% per day.
- Sentiment reversal (e.g., from +1 to -1) triggers a 3–5 day lag correction: reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3 days, then adjust to true trend.
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome is >10% below model, and sentiment is neutral or negative, assume model is overconfident — reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 7 days.
